comment: No source is published. The selector maths runs as follows: the CV is rescaled from the chosen voltage range onto 0 to 1, multiplied by the number of channels less one, has 0.5 added and is truncated, then clamped, so each channel occupies an equal slice of the range and the boundaries fall half way between. The voltage range is a module setting, not a per-jack one, and it is saved with the patch under the key voltageRange; the seven names are spelled exactly as listed, from DigitalAtavism::VoltageRange::GetName, and the limits come from the tables beside it: 0 to 10, 0 to 5, 0 to 1, -10 to 10, -5 to 5, -2.5 to 2.5 and -1 to 1. A new module comes up on the first of them, set by the constructor. The menu item itself is labelled Voltage Range: followed by the current choice, and opens a submenu. Two lights are declared in the call to config() and neither is given a LightWidget or ever written, so nothing on the panel shows them. IN and CV behave differently from each other: a polyphonic CV drives a per-channel switch, while a mono CV places the chosen value on the output channel matching the chosen position rather than on channel 1. No family is given to IN or OUT because they carry whatever is sent through them. Panel lettering came from https://library.vcvrack.com/screenshots/400/DigitalAtavism/UT-P.png; the plugin ships no panel SVG.
